BiblicalUsage: A precious thing is what is desired, and the word is used for the desire of Israel, the desire of women, the desire of all nations, and the goodly raiment Rebekah puts on Jacob. The desire of Israel rests on Saul, the king of the north regards no god but his own will, the nations' desire will come to fill the house, and Rebekah dresses her younger son in his brother's clothes.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe desire is the test of every heart here: Israel desires a king, the king of the north desires only himself, and God promises that the desire of all nations will come. What we desire shows whom we worship.
RelatedEvents: Anointing of Saul as King; Jacob Receives Isaac's Blessing; Rebuilding of the Temple
